44 describes, one afterEach, no shared fixture
Split pays only with the move to the parallel project

label: fanout-run.vitest.ts is 44 top-level describes holding 171 tests with exactly one hook, an afterEach that clears two module-level arrays of temp dirs and hermetic envs, and no beforeAll, shared fixture, require.cache manipulation, global stubbing or process.env mutation.
The file splits cleanly by describe block: each new file needs the same imports and the same afterEach cleanup, and the only shared state is the cleanup list each file would own separately.

A split alone would not help because the serial project sets fileParallelism false and would still run the pieces one at a time, so the split pays only together with the move into the parallel project.
Combined, the move and a four-way split turn 157 s on one worker into roughly 40 s on four workers, which is larger than the whole serial-group saving iteration 2 estimated from moving two files.
The blocks are already sized for a balanced split: max-iterations holds 18 tests, cli-pi 13, and four more hold eight or seven each, so a four-way split need not cut a describe in half.
